After what Inside The Rink called "A Nightmare 2025-26 Season," Kent Johnson has become one of Columbus's most dangerous forwards. He has 16 points in 15 games, including a seven-game point streak, after 22 points in 76 games last year. By our wins-added count, which credits goals by how much they swung the game, he ranks 10th among 504 skaters.

The best reason to believe it is the role. The fifth overall pick in 2021 is playing 17:49 a night, up from 13:14, and is on the ice for 79% of his team's power-play chances, up from 37%. His own chances have climbed too, to 1.07 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.69 (expected goals measure the quality of his looks).

The reason for caution is the finishing. Eight goals on 4.8 expected means he is shooting 24%, after 6% last season, and that rarely lasts. Evolving-Hockey had Columbus creating very little with him on the ice last season; this year his five-on-five numbers are roughly even, which is progress worth watching. Our range puts him at 46 to 69 points by April, a projection that already assumes the shooting cools.
headline: Kent Johnson's breakout is real, his shooting isn't
